phenotype: Gene-expression response to dexamethasone treatment compared with untreated control in primary human airway smooth muscle cells.
cell_type: primary human airway smooth muscle cells
perturbation: 1 micromolar dexamethasone treatment compared with untreated control
study_goal: Identify transcriptional programs and enriched pathways altered by glucocorticoid treatment, prioritize central genes and pathways using network analysis, distinguish plausible dexamethasone-responsive biology from artifacts or nonspecific signals, and recommend follow-up validation experiments.
experimental_design: Paired treatment design using four primary human airway smooth muscle cell lines. Each cell line contributes one untreated sample and one dexamethasone-treated sample, for eight total RNA-seq samples.
biological_background: Dexamethasone is a synthetic glucocorticoid with anti-inflammatory activity. The analysis should focus on glucocorticoid-responsive transcription, inflammatory signaling, extracellular-matrix or contractile programs, and other airway smooth-muscle responses supported by the enrichment evidence.
interpretation_constraints: Treat enrichment, diffusion, follow-up, and consensus scores as prioritization measures rather than new p-values.
Use the original adjusted p-values as the statistical evidence.
Do not assume pathway enrichment proves pathway activation or causal mechanism.
Account for the paired cell-line design when discussing biological variability.
Separate direct evidence from hypotheses and recommended follow-up experiments.
notes: This is the Bioconductor airway demonstration dataset derived from the Himes et al. human airway smooth muscle dexamethasone experiment.
